query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve dynamic strength–ductility performance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an untreated baseline, defines the boundary conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The single intervention that could improve dynamic strength-ductility performance in high-entropy alloys is the introduction of coherent ordered L12 precipitation-strengthenable eutectic high entropy alloy.
generation.intervention: Introduction of coherent ordered L12 precipitation-strengthenable eutectic high entropy alloy
generation.mechanism: Orowan dislocation bowing and by-pass mechanism
generation.boundary: Low temperature annealing and quasi-static or dynamic loading
generation.uncertainty: The effect of the intervention on the strain rate sensitivity (SRS) is not fully understood
generation.falsification_experiment: Testing the alloy under different loading conditions and temperatures to verify the predicted outcome

cited_evidence.text: Recent studies indicate that eutectic high-entropy alloys can simultaneously possess high strength and high ductility, which have potential industrial applications. The present study focuses on Al0.7CoCrFeNi, a lamellar dual-phase (fcc + B2) precipitation-strengthenable eutectic high entropy alloy. This alloy exhibits an fcc + B2 (B2 with bcc nano-precipitates) microstructure resulting in a combination of the soft and ductile fcc phase together with hard B2 phase. Low temperature annealing leads to the precipitation of ordered L12 intermetallic precipitates within the fcc resulting in enhanced strength. The strengthening contribution due to fine scale L12 is modeled using Orowan dislocation bowing and by-pass mechanism. The alloy was tested under quasi-static (strain-rate = 10−3 s−1) tensile loading and dynamic (strain-rate = 103 s−1) compressive loading. Due to the fine lamellar microstructure with a large number of fcc-bcc interfaces, the alloy show relatively high flow-stresses, ~1400 MPa under quasi-static loading and in excess of 1800 MPa under dynamic loading.
